title: create-form-elements.html
content: Create a Form {{snippet.Attendee_AmountRegisterOneTime}} Go to the {{variable.Object_Form}} s tab. Click {{variable.button_new}} . Enter a to create a {{variable.Field_Form_FormName}} . Select a {{variable.Field_Form_Type}} . Click {{variable.Button_Save}} Clone a Form If you need to clone a {{variable.Object_Form}} , click the Clone button on the {{variable.Object_Form}} record you want to clone and follow the steps below to add/edit the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} s. Add Form Elements Relationship Settings and Form Mapping We do not recommend mapping Form Elements to the Attendee object’s {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_FirstName}} , {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_LastName}} , and {{variable.Field_Attendee_Email}} fields. Doing so can create an unsupported process for creating and updating Attendee records. The process of creating an Attendee record includes configured relationship settings. If mapping from a Form to the Attendee object’s {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_FirstName}} , {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_LastName}} , and {{variable.Field_Attendee_Email}} fields occurs, the newly created Contact and/or Account fields will not be populated because the Form mapping disrupts the Attendee record creation process. Click {{variable.Button_AddQuestion}} . Complete the following fields. {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} (required) - select the type of question. For this example, we selected “Pre-registration.” Click here for more information about the different types of questions. {{variable.Field_FormElement_Required}} - select if the question is required. {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} (required) - enter the question. {{variable.Field_FormElement_SuppQuesInfo}} – enter additional information to help an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} answer the question. {{variable.Field_FormElement_MapstoObject}} - define the object where an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} ’s answer will go. {{variable.Field_FormElement_MapstoField}} - define the field on the object where an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} ’s answer will go. {{variable.Field_FormElement_DefaultValue}} - enter the value that will automatically appear on the registration form. {{variable.Field_FormElem_DefaCheckboxVal}} - defines the default value (checked or unchecked) for a checkbox question. {{variable.Field_FormElement_Hint}} - enter information that will help an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} answer the question. {{variable.Field_FormElem_WhenQuestionSho}} select “Always” if there are no additional conditions for this question. Select “When the condition(s) is met” to add conditions and complete the following fields. {{variable.Field_FormElem_AnswerQuestion}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Operator}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Value}} Use the Add Condition button to add more conditions. Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Once you are done creating {{variable.Object_FormElement}} s, your {{variable.Object_Form}} will look similar to the one below. Sorting Form Elements If two questions or Form Elements have the same position, the question added first will be shown first. If you drag and drop questions to change the Sort Order, click {{variable.Button_Save}} to save their new order. When using Events Version 5.0 or higher, use the Forms UI to re-arrange the questions’ (Form Elements) order. Click the {{variable.Button_Form_NewFormElement}} button to add a new {{variable.Object_FormElement}} or reorganize the order of the existing ones. Manually updating the {{variable.Field_BTFrmElmtCond_SortOrder}} field when nested questions are present may result in unexpected behaviors. Form Preview Click the {{variable.Button_Form_FormPreview}} button to see what your {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s will see. Conditional Questions Spaces and Picklist Values When creating multiple Conditional Questions on a Form Element, do NOT add a space after entering a picklist value. Picklist values that include a space after the value will not save properly after an Attendee clicks Save . The answer to a conditional question determines which question ( {{variable.Object_FormElement}} ) will be asked next. This type of question can include multiple levels of nested conditional questions, giving Event Organizers the ability to gather complex information. The following types of {{variable.Object_FormElement}} s allow for conditional questions, including multiple levels of nested conditional questions. A single Form Element can include up to 200 Conditional Form Elements (questions). Checkbox Date Email Multi-Select Picklist Picklist Text Text (30,000) URL Setup Click the {{variable.Button_Form_NewFormElement}} or {{variable.Button_AddQuestion}} button. Complete the following fields. {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} (required) {{variable.Field_FormElement_Required}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} (required) {{variable.Field_FormElement_SuppQuesInfo}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_MapstoObject}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_MapstoField}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_DefaultValue}} {{variable.Field_FormElem_DefaCheckboxVal}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Hint}} In {{variable.Field_FormElem_WhenQuestionSho}} , select “When the condition(s) is met.” Select a question in {{variable.Field_FormElem_AnswerQuestion}} . Choose an {{variable.Field_FormElement_Operator}} . Enter a {{variable.Field_FormElement_Value}} . Click Add Condition if you need to add more conditions. Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Example If you want to find out which sports team is an Attendee’s favorite, but don’t want to use a giant picklist, a conditional question can help narrow down the potential answers. The first question you could ask is, "What is your favorite sport?" Depending on how an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} answers that question, the question, "What is your favorite team" will change. If an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} selects "Baseball," they will see baseball teams. If they select "Football," a list of football teams will be visible. Form Element Types Big List Group (Type Ahead Picklist) {{variable.Object_FormBigListGroup}} s are picklists with thousands of options. Using a {{variable.Object_FormBigListGroup}} gives {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s the option to search for the answer they'd like to select. Setup From the App Launcher, navigate to {{variable.Object_FormBigListGroup}} object. Click {{variable.button_new}} in the top-right-hand corner. Enter a name in the {{variable.Field_FormBigLG_FBigListGrName}} field. Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Example For this example, we will use zip codes. Imagine if an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} had to scroll through thousands of zip codes just to find where they live. That’s very inefficient and a poor {{glossary.user experience}} . By using a {{variable.Object_FormBigListGroup}} , an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} can simply search for their answer and click it. From the App Launcher, navigate to {{variable.Object_FormBigListGroup}} . Click {{variable.button_new}} in the top, right-hand corner. Enter “Zip Codes” in the {{variable.Field_FormBigLG_FBigListGrName}} field. Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Click the Related List tab. Click {{variable.button_new}} next to the {{variable.Object_FormBigListOption}} . Complete the following fields. {{variable.Field_FormBiLOption_OptionName}} : The value that is saved in Salesforce as the answer. {{variable.Field_FormBiLOption_OptionValu}} : The text an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} sees when completing the checkout process. Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Navigate to an existing {{variable.Object_Form}} or create a new one. Create a new {{variable.Object_FormElement}} . Set the {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} field to “Big List Group.” Set the {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} field to “What is your zip code?” Set the {{variable.Field_FormElement_BigListGroup}} field to “Zip Codes.” Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Results The user is asked to enter their zip code. They enter “540” and only see the options that start with “540.” Checkbox Use the “Checkbox” option to ask a question that requires a yes or no answer when you don’t want to create a picklist question. Setup Set the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} field to “Checkbox.” Let {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s know if the question is {{variable.Field_FormElement_Required}} . Enter a {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} that can be answered by clicking a checkbox. In this example, we entered, “Check here if this is your first event.” Complete the remaining fields as needed. Set {{variable.Field_FormElem_WhenQuestionSho}} to “Always.” Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Example Date Use this {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} to ask a question that requires a date for the answer. Setup Set the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} field to “Date.” Let {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s know if the question is {{variable.Field_FormElement_Required}} . Enter a {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} that requires a date for an answer. In this example, we entered, “What is today’s date?” Complete the remaining fields as needed. Set {{variable.Field_FormElem_WhenQuestionSho}} to “Always.” Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Example Dividers Dividers allow Event Organizers to add a blank space between questions or include more information for {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s to see! Setup Set the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} to “Divider.” If you don’t see “Divider in the picklist, go to the Blackthorn | Events Admin tab. Click Upgrade . Click {{variable.Button_ETAdmin_UpdatePicklists}} . Enter the text you want {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s to see in the {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} field. Any text in the {{variable.Field_FormElement_SuppQuesInfo}} field will be displayed at the bottom of the {{variable.Object_Form}} . Set {{variable.Field_FormElem_WhenQuestionSho}} to “Always.” Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Example Email Email questions allow Event Organizers to ask for an email that isn’t included in the Attendee Form. Setup Set the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} field to “Email.” Let {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s know if the question is {{variable.Field_FormElement_Required}} . Enter a {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} that requires an email for an answer. In this example, we entered, “Please enter your student’s email.” Complete the remaining fields as needed. Set {{variable.Field_FormElem_WhenQuestionSho}} to “Always.” Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Example File Upload Uploading files is now part of the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} object. Files can be written to anything in the {{variable.Field_FormElement_MapstoObject}} picklist. After checkout, the file will be uploaded and added to Salesforce Files and the object defined in the {{variable.Field_FormElement_MapstoObject}} picklist. Please keep in mind that files can take up to five minutes to relate to their respective record. Supported File Types All image file formats (for example, .jpg, jpeg, .png, .gif, .svg) and PDF (.pdf). File Access Since only authorized users can access/view the files section in Salesforce, they are the only ones who can access files that are uploaded as part of a Form Element. There can only be one authorized user for Blackthorn Events, which means this user will be listed as the creator of all records (i.e. Attendees, files) created during registration from your Event webpage. All other users must be given specific access to the files under the authorized user. Share Files Uploaded via Form Elements Salesforce offers several ways to share files uploaded via Form Elements with {{variable.Field_BTFormEle_Type}} = “File”. To learn more, select an option on Salesforce’s File Privacy and Sharing document that meets your requirements. Setup Set the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} to “File Upload.” Enter the text you want the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} to see in the {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} field. Files that {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s upload will be added to the Files section of Salesforce. They can also be added as a Related List on the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} / {{variable.Object_Contact}} /etc object that is defined in the {{variable.Field_FormElement_MapstoObject}} picklist. This will allow Event Organizers to easily see the file the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} uploaded. Example Hidden Form Elements To map a hidden {{variable.Object_FormElement}} to a field on a different object, you must assign a default value to the hidden {{variable.Object_FormElement}} . This default value will then map to the configured field after an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} completes the registration process. Examples Map to a Checkbox If you want to map a hidden {{variable.Object_FormElement}} to a checkbox on a different object, set the checkbox’s default value to true. When the {{variable.Object_FormSubmissionAnswer}} is processed, then the checkbox field will be checked. Map to a Text or Picklist Field If you want to map a hidden {{variable.Object_FormElement}} to a text or picklist field on a different object, set the hidden {{variable.Object_FormElement}} ’s {{variable.Field_BTFormEle_DefaultValue}} to the desired text or value. That value will then be mapped to the text or picklist field when the {{variable.Object_FormSubmissionAnswer}} is processed. Multi-Select Picklist Multi-select picklist questions allow Event Organizers to ask questions that can have one or more answers. Setup Set the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} field to “Multi-Select Picklist.” Let {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s know if the question is {{variable.Field_FormElement_Required}} . Enter a {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} that such as “Please select your top two choices.” Enter multiple {{variable.Field_FormEleme_PicklistValues}} . In this example, we are using “Art History,” “Literature,” “Biology,” “Finance,” and “Statistics.” IMPORTANT: Do not add a space after entering a picklist value. Picklist values that include a space after the value will not save properly after an Attendee clicks {{variable.Button_Save}} . Complete the remaining fields as needed. Set {{variable.Field_FormElem_WhenQuestionSho}} to “Always.” Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Example Number Mapping Phone Numbers A value in a Form Element with Type = “Number” cannot be mapped to Phone Number fields in Salesforce. We recommend using a Form Element with Type = “Text” if you need to map a phone number to a Phone Number field. Number questions allow Event Organizers to ask a question that requires a number for an answer. It might be as simple as “How old are you” or complicated like “What is the derivative of 5?” Setup Set the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} field to “Number.” Let {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s know if the question is {{variable.Field_FormElement_Required}} . Enter a {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} such as “How many sides does a square have?” Complete the remaining fields as needed. In this example, the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} is part of a conditional question, so {{variable.Field_FormElem_WhenQuestionSho}} is set to “When the condition(s) is met.” Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Example UTM Parameter UTM Parameters are tags that you can add to a URL. When the link is clicked, the tags are sent back to Google Analytics (or your preferred system) and tracked. The tags are stored in the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s' local storage for 30 days after clicking the {{variable.Object_Event}} link. Setup Set the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} to “Parameter.” Let {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s know if the question is {{variable.Field_FormElement_Required}} . Enter the text in the {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} field. The text entered here will be a part of the original URL. Complete the remaining fields as needed. Set {{variable.Field_FormElem_WhenQuestionSho}} to “Always.” Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Example Parameter question types will not show up in the Additional Information section. Here is an example of a URL that includes the parameter. "https://events.blackthorn.io/en/3h2AhtF7/g/HNex28aSVs/test-all-custom-question-types-4a123hZrGq/overview?utm_param=utm_param_Value" Notice that at the end of the URL, "?utm_param=utm_param_Value," is the text, "utm_param" that was defined in the image above. After the user navigates anywhere in the URL, the “?utm_param=utm_param_Value” disappears from the URL. Even though the text isn't visible, all the information will still be tracked. Picklist Picklist questions allow Event Organizers to present a list of possible answers to their questions. We suggest keeping the list of answers to a manageable amount. For example, scrolling through 20 or 30 options can be frustrating for Attendees. If you need a large number of potential answers, consider using the Big List Group option. Setup Set the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} to “Picklist.” Let {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s know if the question is {{variable.Field_FormElement_Required}} . Enter a {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} such as “Which entrée would you like for lunch?” Enter the following options in the {{variable.Field_FormEleme_PicklistValues}} field: “Chicken,” “Beef,” and “Vegan.” Separate each picklist option with a return or paragraph break. (See the image.) IMPORTANT: Do not add a space after entering a picklist value. Picklist values that include a space after the value will not save properly after an Attendee clicks {{variable.Button_Save}} . Complete the remaining fields as needed. Set {{variable.Field_FormElem_WhenQuestionSho}} to “Always.” Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Example Text Event Organizers should use the Text question when the answer is less than 255 characters. If the answer will be more than 255 characters, use the “Text (30,000)” option. Setup Set the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} to “Text.” Let {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s know if the question is {{variable.Field_FormElement_Required}} . Enter a {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} such as “Please enter five words that describe what it means to be a student.” Complete the remaining fields as needed. Set {{variable.Field_FormElem_WhenQuestionSho}} to “Always.” Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Example Text (30,000) If an Attendee’s answer will be more than 255 characters, Event Organizers must use the “Text (30,000)” option. Setup Set the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} to “Text (30,000).” Let {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s know if the question is {{variable.Field_FormElement_Required}} . Enter a {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} such as “Please describe your experience as a student in less than 500 words.” Complete the remaining fields as needed. Set {{variable.Field_FormElem_WhenQuestionSho}} to “Always.” Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Example URL The URL option allows {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s to enter a URL upon registration. This field will validate that the text entered is a proper URL. When written to a URL Salesforce field, the text will appear as a hyperlink. When written to a text field, the text will appear as text with no hyperlink. Setup Set the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} field to “URL.” Let {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s know if the question is {{variable.Field_FormElement_Required}} . In the {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} field, enter the text you want the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} to see. If necessary, define the {{variable.Field_FormElement_SuppQuesInfo}} , {{variable.Field_FormElement_DefaultValue}} , and {{variable.Field_FormElement_Hint}} fields. Set {{variable.Field_FormElem_WhenQuestionSho}} to “Always.” Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Example When an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} enters data into a URL field, the system will validate that the text starts with http:// or https:// and has a top-level domain (.com, .gov, .io,. etc.) identified. Post-Registration Forms {{variable.Object_Form}} s with {{variable.Field_Form_Type}} set to “Post-registration” use {{variable.AttendeeLink}} s to gather information. Once an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} registers for an {{variable.Object_Event}} or is invited to an {{variable.Object_Event}} , they'll receive their {{variable.AttendeeLink}} via email. The {{variable.AttendeeLink}} can include the post-registration questions. Setup Go to the Forms tab. Click {{variable.button_new}} . Set {{variable.Object_Form}} {{variable.Field_Form_Type}} to “Post-registration.” Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Complete the following fields to create the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} . {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} (required) - Select the question type you want to use. {{variable.Field_FormElement_Required}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_QuestiontoAs}} (required) {{variable.Field_FormElement_SuppQuesInfo}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_MapstoObject}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_MapstoField}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_DefaultValue}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Hint}} Set {{variable.Field_FormElem_WhenQuestionSho}} to “Always.” Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Go to the {{variable.Object_Event}} record. Add the {{variable.Object_Form}} to the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_FormPostRegistra}} field on the {{variable.Object_Event}} . {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s will now see the questions when they revisit their {{variable.AttendeeLink}} . Unlike pre-registration {{variable.Object_Form}} s, {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s won’t see any prefilled fields. Example Change the Text The generic text that appears on the post-registration Form is “Thank you for attending [XYZ]. Please take a few moments to answer our survey." If you want to change the original text, use the MSG_SURVEY_TITLE {{variable.Field_DataDictionary_Key}} from the Blackthorn Events Data Dictionary document. Click here for more information about the Data Dictionary feature. Post-Event Survey Post-Event Surveys/Questions can now be translated. However, please note the following. Default values, picklist values, and big list values will not be translated to accommodate custom flows and logic. Since Post-Event Questions can work independently from Events/Event Settings, they are not impacted by the Event Settings’ {{variable.Field_ETETSettings_SourceLangu}} field. Instead, the questions will be written in the language set by the org’s locale. Post-event surveys allow {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s to give feedback on an {{variable.Object_Event}} . They can be added to {{variable.Object_Event}} , {{variable.Object_EventItem}} , and {{variable.Object_Attendee}} records. We recommend using the process builder or flows to set up a process to automatically send the {{variable.Field_Attendee_PostEvTQuestURL}} . Complete the following steps to add a post-event survey. Go to the {{variable.Object_Form}} s tab. Click {{variable.button_new}} . Fill in the following fields. {{variable.Field_Form_FormName}} (required) {{variable.Field_Form_Type}} = “Survey.” Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Add one or more {{variable.Object_FormElement}} s to the survey. Go to relevant {{variable.Object_Event}} , {{variable.Object_EventItem}} , or {{variable.Object_Attendee}} record and add the previously created {{variable.Object_Form}} to the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_PostEventQuestio}} field. Note: The {{variable.Field_Attendee_PostEvTQuestURL}} is unique to {{variable.Object_Attendee}} record. The field pulls from the {{variable.Object_Form}} added to the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_PostEventQuestio}} field on the {{variable.Object_Event}} , {{variable.Object_EventItem}} , or {{variable.Object_Attendee}} records. Sessions The same functionality applies at the Session level. The {{variable.Field_ETEvent_PostEventQuestio}} field can be found on both the {{variable.Object_Session}} and {{variable.Object_SessionAttendee}} records. The {{variable.Object_SessionAttendee}} record also includes the {{variable.Field_SessionAtten_PostSesQURL}} , just like its {{variable.Object_Attendee}} record counterpart. FAQ Q: How do we automatically send the {{variable.Object_Form}} ’s URL to ONLY the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s who actually attended? A: Use the Email component to create and send an {{variable.Object_EmailTemplate}} with the {{variable.Field_Attendee_PostEvTQuestURL}} and the Attendee Filter set to {{variable.Field_Attendee_AttendancStatus}} = “Attended.” View Attendee Answers Dietary Preference Field Mapping The Dietary Preference field on the Attendee object is automatically set to map to the {{variable.Field_EventItem_DietaryPrefer}} field on the Event Item. As a result, the Attendee's Dietary Preference field does not work with custom Forms. {{variable.Object_Form}} s are submitted to Salesforce through the {{variable.Object_ET_FormSubmission}} object. There are two Related Lists that can be added on the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} object to easily access an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} 's answers: Form Submission & Form Submission Answer. Navigate to the Form Submissions Related List, and click the {{variable.Field_FrmSub_FormSubmissionNam}} you want to view, or Navigate to the Form Submission Answer Related List and click the specific answer you want to view. If a specific {{variable.Object_ET_Abb_FormSubmission}} fails to process, open the {{variable.Object_ET_FormSubmission}} , and click the {{variable.Button_Process}} button. This will reprocess the answers and submit the {{variable.Object_Form}} properly. The following {{variable.Object_FormElement}} types do not map to the {{variable.Field_FormSubAns_Answer}} field on the {{variable.Object_FormSubmissionAnswer}} object. For the types that do not map to the {{variable.Field_FormSubAns_Answer}} field, see the mappings below. {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} = “Date” maps to the {{variable.Object_FormSubmissionAnswer}} {{variable.Field_FormSubAnswer_AnswerDate}} field. {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} = “Number” maps to the {{variable.Object_FormSubmissionAnswer}} {{variable.Field_FormSubAnswer_AnswerNumb}} field. {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} = “Multi-Select Picklist” maps to the {{variable.Object_FormSubmissionAnswer}} {{variable.Field_FormSubAnswer_AnswTxtLon}} field. {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} = "Text (30,000)" maps to the {{variable.Object_FormSubmissionAnswer}} {{variable.Field_FormSubAnswer_AnswTxtLon}} field. {{variable.Object_FormElement}} {{variable.Field_FormElement_Type}} = “Big List Group” maps to the {{variable.Object_FormSubmissionAnswer}} {{variable.Field_FormSubAnswer_FormBigLis}} field.
